title: A Bengaluru robotics startup wants to build a factory that can make anything
sources: The Robot Report - CynLr raises Series A funding to realize robot vision for universal factory
Tech Funding News - CynLr cements $10M in Series A funding led by key venture partners to drive robotic automation in manufacturing
caption:
Most factory robots can only do one job, on one object, forever. One Bengaluru startup built a robot that can pick up almost anything, untrained.

CynLr's $10 million Series A round, led by Pavestone and Athera Venture Partners, brings total funding to $15.2 million. Its CyRo robot uses 'visual object sentience' to manipulate objects without prior training. Founded in 2019, the company is expanding from 60 to 120 people across India, the US and Switzerland, aiming to deploy one robot a day and reach $22 million in revenue by 2027.

Most manufacturing robots are built for one line, one product, one repetition. A robot that can handle anything is a bet that factories themselves are about to change shape.
